## Findings
- claim-1: For \(r,q\ge1\), with \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\) the \(q^r\)-box quotient, \[ A\cong\mathbb Z[h_1,\ldots,h_q]/(e_{r+1},\ldots,e_{r+q}), \] where \(E(-t)H(t)=1\). Indeed, \[ I_{r,q}=(h_{q+1},h_{q+2},\ldots,e_{r+1},\ldots,e_{r+q}). \]
- claim-2: For the \(i=j=1\) case, \(J_v=A_+\), and, with \(m=\min(r,q)\), \[ A_+/A_+^2\cong\bigoplus_{k=1}^{m}\mathbb Z\,\overline h_k\cong\mathbb Z^m. \]
- claim-3: In \(A_+/A_+^2\), \[ \overline e_k=(-1)^{k-1}\overline h_k\qquad(1\le k\le m). \] Hence both \(\{h_1,\ldots,h_m\}\) and \(\{e_1,\ldots,e_m\}\) map to integral bases.
- claim-4: The two specialized families are \[ \{h_1,\ldots,h_m\},\qquad \{e_1,\ldots,e_m\}; \] each minimally generates \(J_v=A_+\). Thus the \(i=j=1\) family, equivalently \(v_{r,r,r,r+q}\) for \(r,q\ge1\), is settled.
- claim-5: The supplied project documentation records the corresponding free-indecomposables assertion as only suspected in the general rectangular case. [source-6@L56-L70|claim=ordinary-document]
## Strategy
Let \(q=n-r\), \(P=\mathbb Z[h_1,\ldots,h_q]\), and define \(e_k\in P\) by
\[
E(-t)H(t)=1,\qquad H(t)=1+h_1t+\cdots+h_qt^q.
\]
Prove the box presentation
\[
A=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\cong P/(e_{r+1},\ldots,e_{r+q}).
\]
Indeed, after \(h_{>q}=0\), the recurrence
\[
e_N-h_1e_{N-1}+h_2e_{N-2}-\cdots+(-1)^qh_qe_{N-q}=0
\quad(N>q)
\]
shows inductively that \(e_{r+1},\ldots,e_{r+q}\) imply \(e_N=0\) for every \(N>r\). For a partition outside \(q^r\), ordinary Jacobi--Trudi, expanded along its first row
\[
(h_{\lambda_1},h_{\lambda_1+1},\ldots,h_{\lambda_1+\ell(\lambda)-1}),
\]
puts \(s_\lambda\) in \((h_{q+1},h_{q+2},\ldots)\) if \(\lambda_1>q\). If \(\ell(\lambda)>r\), dual Jacobi--Trudi has matrix
\[
(e_{\lambda'_i-i+j})_{1\le i,j\le\lambda_1};
\]
its first row has indices \(\lambda'_1,\lambda'_1+1,\ldots\), all \(>r\), so expansion puts \(s_\lambda\) in \((e_{r+1},e_{r+2},\ldots)\).

Put \(P_+=(h_1,\ldots,h_q)\). Then
\[
A_+/A_+^2\cong P_+/(P_+^2+(e_{r+1},\ldots,e_{r+q})).
\]
Modulo \(P_+^2\),
\[
e_N\equiv
\begin{cases}
(-1)^{N-1}h_N,&N\le q,\\
0,&N>q.
\end{cases}
\]
Thus the only linear relations are the unit-coordinate relations
\[
h_{r+1}=\cdots=h_q=0
\]
when \(r<q\). Hence, for \(m=\min(r,q)\),
\[
A_+/A_+^2\cong \bigoplus_{k=1}^m\mathbb Z\,\overline h_k\cong\mathbb Z^m.
\]
Taking degree-\(k\) coefficients in \(E(-t)H(t)=1\) further gives
\[
\overline e_k=(-1)^{k-1}\overline h_k\qquad(1\le k\le m).
\]

Under the stipulated identification \(J_v=A_+\), graded Nakayama applies to the bounded-below graded \(A\)-module \(A_+\): both \(\{h_1,\ldots,h_m\}\) and \(\{e_1,\ldots,e_m\}\) map to integral bases of \(A_+/A_+^2\), hence each minimally generates \(A_+\).

Finally, the parameter formulas \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\) give \(i=j=1\) precisely for
\[
s=t=r,\qquad n=r+q,
\]
namely \(v_{r,r,r,r+q}\).

## Gaps
- This proof is conditional on the task’s stated specialization \(J_v=A_+\) and on the standard box-quotient description of \(A\).
- The \(e_k\) in the polynomial presentation must consistently denote their specialized images in \(\mathbb Z[h_1,\ldots,h_q]\).
- No claim is made for rectangles other than \(1^1\).

## Next
- Independently check the Jacobi--Trudi ideal-containment argument and the recurrence signs.
- Incorporate the proof as the \(i=j=1\) uniform special case, retaining the general rectangular case as unresolved.
